close_reason: FALSE ALARM: matches_dns_name without leading dot matches subdomains (test 30 passes)
description: matches_dns_name lines 973-980: when constraint has no leading period, the comment says 'matches exact host AND any subdomain'. But RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 text says: 'DNS name constraint without a leading period matches the host and any subdomain'. However PKITS 4.13.30 is ignored with the note 'DNS subdomain match not implemented; exact match only'. But lines 976-980 DO attempt subdomain matching. The real failure of test 30 (subject=testserver.testcertificates.gov, constraint=testcertificates.gov) should pass: subject.len() > constraint.len() + 1 (30 > 20 + 1 = 21, YES), subject.as_bytes()[30-20-1=9] should be '.'. Let me verify: 'testserver.testcertificates.gov'[9] = '.'. So subject[9..] = '.testcertificates.gov'. eq_ignore_ascii_case('testcertificates.gov'). This checks subject[11..] not subject[9..]. Actually subject[subject.len()-constraint.len()..] = subject[11..] = 'testcertificates.gov'. That DOES equal constraint. The subdomain condition: subject.as_bytes()[subject.len()-constraint.len()-1] = subject.as_bytes()[10] = '.' — yes. So this SHOULD match. Test 30 may be failing for a different reason (possibly the check is on a SAN vs subject). This needs deeper investigation but the bug comment on test 30 appears to be stale/wrong — the matching logic looks correct for straight subdomain. Worth investigating why test 30 actually fails.
title: matches_dns_name: no-leading-dot does NOT match subdomains per RFC 5280
